description:
The Pentagon said Thursday it will livestream the military’s first firing squad execution since 1945, allowing the public to watch as the man who killed 13 people in a 2009 mass shooting at Fort Hood is put to death.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth vowed in an interview this week to let the public watch a firing squad execute Nidal Hasan at the same base in Texas where he carried out the massacre. “We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public, because people need to understand that there’s serious consequences for these types of things,” Hegseth told far-right podcaster Jack Posobiec in an interview aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln on Wednesday, drawing swift backlash from both sides of the aisle.

CNN senior national security reporter Haley Britzsky reports on the Pentagon's plan, and Audie Cornish rounds up reaction online and in her "CNN This Morning" Group Chat

0:47 Pentagon announcement sparks
title: Pentagon to livestream Ft. Hood shooter’s firing squad execution

description:
Isaias has strengthened into a Category 3 hurricane with sustained winds of 120 mph, according to a special update from the National Hurricane Center. That makes it a major hurricane, a designation reserved for storms rated Category 3 or higher. 

Current forecasts call for the storm to hit east of New Orleans, a major refining hub, which should spare vital energy infrastructure from the storm’s worst. 

Still, major oil producers including Shell, Chevron and BP have evacuated non-essential personnel from oil platforms in the Gulf and curtailed production.

CNN meteorologist Allison Chinchar has the details and CNN’s Audie Cornish speaks with Bloomberg News oil products reporter Will Kubzansky about the impact on US oil production. Also, CNN’s Rafael Romo reports on conditions in Pensacola, Florida, and Fairhope, Alabama, Mayor Sherry Sullivan says she is most concerned about potential storm surge.
